chunks: From Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from some of his companions, he raised it (to the Imam) saying:

While Musa (peace be upon him) was walking along the seashore, a fisherman came and prostrated himself to the sun, speaking with polytheism. Then he cast his net and drew it out full. He cast it again and drew it out full. He cast it again and drew out the same until he was satisfied, then he departed. Then another man came, performed ablution, stood in prayer, praised Allah and glorified Him. Then he cast his net but it brought out nothing. He cast it again and it brought out nothing. He cast it again and a small fish came out. He praised Allah and glorified Him and departed. Musa said: 'O Lord, Your servant came and denied You, prayed to the sun and spoke with polytheism, then cast his net and drew it out full, then cast it again and drew it out full, then cast it again and drew out the same until he was satisfied and departed. And Your believing servant came, performed ablution and perfected it, then prayed, praised, supplicated and glorified, then cast his net and brought out nothing, then cast it again and brought out nothing, then cast it again and brought out a small fish, so he praised You and departed?'

So Allah revealed to him: 'O Musa, look to your right.' Musa looked and it was revealed to him what Allah had prepared for His believing servant, so he looked. Then it was said to him: 'O Musa, look to your left.' And it was revealed to him what Allah had prepared for His disbelieving servant, so he looked. Then Allah the Almighty said: 'O Musa, what was given to this one did not benefit him, and what was withheld from that one did not harm him.' Musa said: 'O Lord, it is fitting for one who knows You to be content with what You have done.'
ai.seo_question: What is the lesson of the fisherman's net in the hadith of Musa?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an incident where Prophet Musa (peace be upon him) observes a polytheist fisherman and a believing fisherman. The polytheist, despite his disbelief, catches abundant fish, while the believer catches only a small fish. Allah reveals to Musa that the polytheist's abundance did not benefit him in the hereafter, and the believer's scarcity did not harm him, illustrating the concept of divine decree and the distinction between worldly provision and spiritual reward.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 14. It has been narrated from Ibn Abu 'Umayr through some of his companions that he said:

Prophet Musa (a.s) was once walking along the sea shore when a fisherman came by and prostrated himself before the Sun, uttering words of polytheism. Then he threw his fishing net in (to the sea) and drew it out filled (with fish). Then he threw it in again and once again it came out full. Once more he repeated this and once again it came out full until he was satisfied then he departed. Then another man came along, performed the ablution and stood in prayer, praising and glorifying Allah. Then he flung his net in but drew it back empty. So he repeated it and again he met with no success. Once again, he threw his net in and this time he caught a small fish. So, he praised and thanked Allah and went off. Seeing this, Musa (a.s) called out, 'O Lord! When Your servant came along and denied You, praying to the Sun and uttering blasphemy, his net was filled in with fish repeatedly until he was satisfied and left. And when Your believing servant came along, performed the ablution, prayed, glorified, praised and supplicated to You and then threw his net in, he received nothing but a small fish?'

So, Allah [M.G] revealed to him, 'O Musa! Look to your right.' Musa looked and it was revealed to him what Allah [M.G] had set aside (in reward) for the believing servant. Then it was said to him, 'O Musa, now look to your left.' And he saw what (punishment) was awaiting the disbelieving servant. Then Allah [M.G] spoke, 'O Musa, (in reality) the one whom I gave did not benefit anything and nor did the one I denied lose anything.'' O Lord!' responded Musa (a.s), '(Indeed) it is the duty of all that know You to be content with whatever You do (for them).'
